_README: Committed baseline for the agent memory verification suite.
Gated by tests/memverify/test_o_baseline.py via tests/memverify/metrics.py.
Each entry is {"min": n} or {"max": n}. A bound of null means the number
has NEVER been measured; that is reported as a FAILURE, not tolerated, and
the failure message prints the JSON to paste back here. A number nobody has
looked at must not read as a pass — that is the defect this whole change
exists to fix.
`source` records where a bound came from, so a modelled figure can never be
mistaken for a measured one:
contract  - restates an assertion the suite already makes elsewhere.
invariant - follows from the production code, not from a measurement.
measured  - observed on a real run; `recorded_at` names that run.
unrecorded- bound is null; the next real run must record it.
2026-08-07: THE SUITE HAS NOW RUN. The OPENAI_API_KEY secret this file's
previous note described as missing was added, and the suite executed end to
end for the first time since it landed: 165 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped.
The single failure was this file doing its job — unlabeled_rate_pct had no
bound, so it reported the measured value and refused to pass.
unlabeled_rate_pct is now recorded, but NOT at the first value observed.
The extractor is an LLM, so the number moves between runs, and a ratchet
pinned to one sample is worse than no ratchet: it flaps, someone widens it
under time pressure, and the gate stops meaning anything. Seven consecutive
clean-state runs on 2026-08-07 measured:
So both terms move: 3-5 catch-all rows over a denominator of 75-80, mean
3.57 rows (sd 0.79). A bound at the first sample (3.75) would have failed
six of those seven runs. The ceiling is set at 8.0%, which tolerates up to
6 catch-all rows at the smallest observed denominator — roughly three
standard deviations above the mean — and still fails a genuine regression,
where extraction degrading to 7+ catch-all rows means the real extractor has
started reaching for the bucket that carries no usable label. Tighten it
when there are enough runs to justify a tighter number; do not widen it
without recording why here.
non_canonical_rate_pct measured 0.0 on all seven runs, confirming the
invariant its bound was already derived from.

recall_pct.note: test_a_capture_recall.py::test_recall_aggregate already asserts recall == 1.0. Restated here so all three headline numbers are gated in one place. First real run measured 100.0 (32 of 32 facts), confirming the contract rather than replacing it.

precision_pct.note: test_b_precision_junk.py::test_junk_aggregate already asserts zero junk across ALL_LABELED. 100% precision is the same statement as a junk count of 0. First real run measured 100.0 (0 of 44 junk markers stored).

non_canonical_rate_pct.note: Every production write path normalises the category before it reaches the column - memory_service.py:536, memory_extractor.py:872 and :1131, agent_reflection.py:168. A row whose stored value is not canonical for its brain means a path bypassed normalize_category, which is a structural defect independent of extraction quality. Measured 0.0 on all seven 2026-08-07 runs.

unlabeled_rate_pct.note: Seven consecutive clean-state runs 2026-08-07 measured 3.75, 3.85, 3.90, 4.00, 5.06, 5.26 and 6.67 percent (3-5 catch-all rows over 75-80 stored rows; mean 3.57 rows, sd 0.79). Bound set at 8.0 rather than at the observed maximum: this is an LLM-driven number and a ceiling inside its own jitter would flap. 8.0 tolerates 6 catch-all rows at the smallest observed denominator and still catches a doubling. See _README before changing it.
